title: Light-Dependent Reactions (Z-Scheme)
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AP Biology
description: Interactive step-through MicroSim showing electron flow through the Z-scheme of photosynthesis light reactions

learningObjectives: Trace the path of an electron from water through PSII, ETC, and PSI to NADPH
Identify each carrier molecule and the direction of proton pumping
Explain where ATP and NADPH are produced in the light reactions

keyQuestions: Why does the Z-scheme have two upward energy jumps?
Where is the proton gradient generated?
How does the proton gradient drive ATP synthesis?
commonMisconceptions: Light reactions only occur in the presence of visible light
PSII comes after PSI (PSII was named second but acts first)
ATP is produced directly by the photosystems
assessmentOpportunities: Trace electron path from H2O to NADPH
Explain the role of each complex in the thylakoid membrane
